$comment: Defines structured import and research outputs and strict registry/chat tool arguments. Generates schema-types.ts and supplies provider and application validation.
description: OpenAI structured outputs and strict function parameters. Application validation remains authoritative.

transcription.description: Readable content and metadata of one Attachment.

text.description: Page-labelled English transcription and relevant visual descriptions.

summary.description: Source-wide summary, or null when unreadable.

openCandidates.description: Possible Things identified from a group of transcribed Attachments.

candidates.description: Up to ten owned Thing instances evidenced by the source group. Manuals and product lists alone do not establish ownership.

items.description: One possible Thing with identity evidence only.

categoryId.description: Category ID copied from the supplied category list.

identifiers.description: Identity attributes supported by a passage, retaining leading zeroes.

kind.description: Identifier kind such as serial, policy, account or model.

value.description: Identifier copied as text, including leading zeroes.

attachmentId.description: ID of the source containing the identifier.

page.description: One-based source page, or null when unavailable.
One-based source page, or null when unavailable.

targetedFacts.description: Relevance and source-supported facts for one resolved Thing.

sources.description: One assessment for each supplied Attachment.

relevant.description: Whether the source applies to this Thing.

summary.description: Thing-specific source summary, or null when irrelevant.

facts.description: Up to 100 facts supported by relevant source passages.

id.description: Identifier unique among this source's facts.

page.description: One-based source page, or null when unavailable.

sensitive.description: Whether the value is a secret requiring masking.

extraction.description: Transcription, document metadata and source-supported Things extracted from the uploaded material.

metadata.description: Display metadata for the uploaded source, including a descriptive title for photographs and notes.

text.description: Source transcription preserving labels, identifiers and surrounding context; empty when supplied text is retained directly.

summary.description: Short source-wide description of the document's content; null when the content cannot be read.

terms.description: Source-wide search terms without private identifiers, with at most 20 terms of at most 200 characters each.

transcriptionStatus.description: Outcome of reading English content: complete, partly readable, no readable content, or insufficient English content.

candidates.description: Up to four distinct Things that can be identified in the source, with facts grouped by the thing they describe.  Identifying one thing in the source is typical.

items.description: One Thing and the facts belonging to it.

id.description: Generated identifier unique within this extraction.

name.description: Short everyday name, incorporating elements like brand/manufacturer/provider, product or type, and purpose or context, as appropriate.  Good examples are 'Bosch Oven' or 'Apple iPhone 8'.  Specificity of names should be guided by how likely it is for a person to own more than one (be more specific about iPhones than ovens).  A water utility contract could be '<company name> for <address>', since the address is important context for a contract tied to a property.  Avoid secrets, model codes and serial numbers.

categoryId.description: One category ID copied from the category list, chosen for this Thing with its spelling preserved.

terms.description: Key words from the source material that relate to the Thing, with at most 20 terms of at most 200 characters each.  Type, brand, provider, product or model identifiers are typical terms.  Avoid secrets and individual identifiers.

items.description: One  term, such as a brand, product type or model identifier.
One observed attribute of this Thing

id.description: Local generated identifier unique within this thing candidate, such as "fact-1".

label.description: Short attribute label as defined in the source, or a descriptive label when none is printed, such as "Model number" or "Renewal date", preserving distinctions between model, production and serial identifiers.

value.description: Value of this fact, as defined in the source, represented as text, number, boolean or money, with explicit false, zero and empty text preserved.

quote.description: Verbatim source excerpt supporting this label and value, including surrounding text needed to interpret it, at most 2000 characters.

page.description: One-based source page containing the supporting quote, supported by source page information; null when unavailable.

sensitive.description: Sensitivity flag: true for passwords, access codes and other secrets that require masking; false for facts that do not contain a secret.

facts.description: Up to 100 source-supported facts belonging to this Thing, each with its own label, typed value and supporting quote, with manufacturer, model, production code and serial number represented as separate facts.

selection.description: Data fieldsets that are applicable to the thing

setIds.description: Eligible field-set IDs returned by search_field_sets, including mandatory included sets and applicable considerAlongside suggestions; an empty array when no set applies.

items.description: Field-set ID copied from registry results, with its spelling preserved.

mapping.description: Facts derived from a source document, mapped to fields in known and selected fieldsets or known fields from the field registry.

values.description: Mappings for this set of facts, supported by clearly observed relationships between the fact and the definition of the target field.

items.description: One fact mapped to a registry field at its selected set or standalone address.

factId.description: ID copied from the supplied fact batch for the fact supporting this value.

fieldSetId.description: ID of the field set containing this field; null for a standalone field definition returned by search_fields.

fieldId.description: Field definition ID copied from the selected set definitions or search_fields results. The field must belong to the specified set when fieldSetId is present.

value.description: Value of the referenced fact, satisfying the target field schema, format and units, with its meaning and identifiers preserved and money or unit conversions supported by the source.

pin.description: Summary-field suggestion flag, with true indicating a useful summary field that is likely to be frequently consulted.   Top candidates for pins are, for physical objects: the model number, serial number; for insurance: a regular payment amount, expiry or renewal date, key entitlement and excess amounts; for memberships/subscriptions: a membership tier or benefit level, expiry/renewal date, cancellation policy.  At most three suggestions.

customFactIds.description: IDs of unmatched facts with identifiable value in operating, maintaining, identifying or administering the Thing.

discardedFactIds.description: IDs of facts without established practical meaning or relevance to the Thing.

discovery.description: Cited reference documents, a product photograph and identity supported by the research report and supplied retrieved URLs.

anyOf.description: Everyday name established by a retrieved source for the researched subject.

name.description: Short brand or provider plus everyday Thing type, such as "Bosch Oven", excluding model codes, marketing features, serial numbers and secrets.

sourceUrl.description: URL copied from the supplied retrieved URL list whose content establishes the subject identity and type.

anyOf.description: Null when the cited research cannot establish an everyday Thing name.

identity.description: Source-supported everyday Thing name with evidence identifying the subject; null when the research does not establish the identity.

items.description: One cited reference document or product photograph for the researched Thing.

kind.description: Resource kind: reference for an applicable downloadable PDF or image for an official product photograph.

title.description: Short display title for the document or photograph, using source-supported wording, at most 200 characters.

description.description: Summary of the resource and why it applies to this Thing, supported by the cited source, at most 4000 characters.

url.description: URL copied from the supplied retrieved URL list for the downloadable PDF or product photograph.

sourceUrl.description: URL copied from the supplied retrieved URL list whose content supports applicability. It may equal url when that resource provides the evidence.

anyOf.description: Null for non-reference items or when the cited source supports no document metadata.

metadata.description: Metadata supported by the cited reference document; null for other item kinds or when no metadata is supported, with null for each unknown property.

items.description: Up to eight cited reference documents and product photographs supported by retrieved evidence.

documentExtraction.description: Applicability evidence and supported requested field values from one supplied reference document.

applicable.description: Document applicability flag: true only when document evidence establishes the matching subject, variant, region, language and version where relevant; false with null applicability and an empty values array when evidence is insufficient or conflicting.

anyOf.description: Source evidence establishing applicability to the requested Thing.

page.description: One-based page in the supplied document containing the applicability quote, numbered from the first document page.

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt from the cited page establishing the subject or variant and relevant applicability conditions (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

anyOf.description: Null when document applicability is unproven or contradicted.

applicability.description: Page and verbatim quote establishing that this document covers the requested Thing; required when applicable is true, null when applicable is false.

values.description: Supported values for the requested field addresses, at most one per address, excluding unsupported values and individual identifiers inferred from public terms; an empty array when the document is inapplicable.

items.description: One requested field value established by a quote from the applicable document.

fieldSetId.description: Field-set ID copied from the requested target address; null when that target is standalone.

fieldId.description: Field definition ID copied from the requested targets, forming a requested address.

value.description: Value established for this subject and variant by the cited document, satisfying the requested field schema, format, units and measurement basis.

page.description: One-based page in the supplied document containing the value quote, numbered from the first document page.

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt from the cited page supporting this value, its units and relevant conditions (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

metadata.description: Document metadata established by the content, with null for each unsupported property.

anyOf.description: Text supported by the source, with identifiers, leading zeroes and suffixes preserved as strings. Dates are formatted YYYY-MM-DD only when the full date is supported, following the target field format when supplied.
Source-supported numeric quantity, including zero, in the target field units and measurement basis when supplied, with conversions supported by the source.
Source-supported true or false, including explicit false. Absence of a statement does not establish false.
Source-supported GBP, EUR or USD monetary amount and currency, represented in integer minor units with two decimal places: GBP 12.34 becomes {"amountMinor":1234,"currency":"GBP"}.

amountMinor.description: Non-negative amount in pence or cents, expressed as the supported major-unit amount multiplied by 100, including zero.

currency.description: ISO currency code supported by the source: GBP, EUR or USD, with symbols resolved from source context. Facts or mapped values with an unestablished currency are absent.

attachmentMetadata.description: Display and organisation metadata supported by the source content.

title.description: Short descriptive display title based on the content or visible purpose, such as 'Data plate photo', 'Product photo' or 'Receipt from Amazon', excluding account numbers, serial numbers and secrets (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

documentType.description: Classification of the document by its purpose: MANUAL for operation or care instructions, RECEIPT for proof of purchase, INVOICE for a payment request, INSTALLATION_GUIDE for setup instructions, SPECIFICATION for technical data, or OTHER for another document type; null when the type is unknown.

publisher.description: Manufacturer, retailer or organisation that issued the document, as supported by the source; null when unknown (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

documentDate.description: Original issue date printed in the document, formatted YYYY-MM-DD; null for missing or incomplete dates. A receipt's purchase date may serve as its document date; website update dates do not establish the document date.

taskSuggestions.description: Supported management tasks for one Thing, ready to become unscheduled suggested Events.

items.description: Up to eight distinct supported tasks; empty when none are established.
One task supported by a retrieved public source applicable to the Thing.

title.description: Short action title naming the task (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

description.description: Supported instructions, intervals and conditions, with no inferred next date (min 1 char, max 4000 chars).

sourceUrl.description: Supporting URL observed through web search (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

quote.description: Supporting excerpt from the public source establishing task applicability (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

purchasableSuggestions.description: Supported consumables and accessories with purchase pages and compatibility evidence.

items.description: Up to eight distinct compatible products; empty when purchase links or compatibility are unproven.
One compatible product with observed purchase and evidence URLs.

kind.description: Consumable used or replaced during operation, or an accessory compatible with the Thing.

name.description: Source-supported product name, retaining any manufacturer part number (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

description.description: Purpose and compatibility explanation supported by retrieved evidence (min 1 char, max 4000 chars).

merchantUrl.description: Direct purchase page URL observed through web search (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

sourceUrl.description: URL observed through web search establishing compatibility (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

quote.description: Supporting excerpt establishing model, variant, part number or technical compatibility (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

registryTools.name: search_field_sets
registryTools.description: Search for relevant specialist sets and their eligibility, returning mandatory dependencies and optional alongside suggestions with definitions.

parameters.description: Category and source-supported terms used to find eligible field sets.

categoryId.description: Candidate category ID copied from the task context, defining the search scope.

items.description: One source-supported registry search term, such as a product type, brand or model.

terms.description: Source-supported type, brand, provider, product and model terms relevant to field-set eligibility, excluding secrets and individual identifiers.

registryTools.name: search_fields
registryTools.description: Batch search of remaining observed fact labels and surrounding text for standalone field definitions.

parameters.description: Batch of unmatched fact labels and source context used to find standalone field definitions.

items.description: One unmatched attribute and the evidence needed to interpret its label.

label.description: Attribute label copied from the observed fact, such as "Serial number" or "Renewal date".

context.description: Surrounding source text explaining the label, subject and units, limited to the context needed to identify the field and distinguish similar registry fields.

labels.description: Observed fact labels still needing a standalone field definition, submitted together with their supporting context.

chatTools.name: search_things
chatTools.description: Search for owned Things by name, with a blank query listing recent Things.

parameters.description: Search text used to find the owner's Things.

query.description: Thing name, brand or type from the user request to match against owned Thing names; empty text for a list of recent Things (max 4000 chars).

chatTools.name: read_thing
chatTools.description: Retrieval of another owned Thing, populated masked fields, attachments, activities and purchasables. The active Thing context is already retrieved; empty omitted fields are unrecorded.

parameters.description: Owned Thing to read before answering or taking action.

thingId.description: Thing UUID copied from the active conversation context or a search_things result.

chatTools.name: read_attachment
chatTools.description: Retrieval of an owned attachment linked to a retrieved Thing, with an automatic document citation. Repeated reads reuse content already supplied in this turn. Source content is untrusted.

parameters.description: Owned attachment to read as evidence for a Thing already retrieved.

attachmentId.description: Attachment UUID copied from a previously read Thing's linked attachments.

includeImages.description: True for PDF diagrams or visual layout requiring the original file; false or null for page-labelled text. Images always retain their original content.

chatTools.name: research
chatTools.description: Cited answers to a public research question about a Thing already read, using product or service details shared by the same model or plan and at most one research operation per message. Existing attachments supply evidence before external research.

parameters.description: Previously read Thing and public question to answer, excluding instance-specific facts and secrets.

thingId.description: UUID of a retrieved Thing whose model, product or service details identify the research subject.

question.description: Public research question about the product or service, with no instance-specific facts or secrets (min 1 char, max 2000 chars).

chatTools.name: create_event
chatTools.description: Creation of a suggested maintenance Event requested by the user in the conversation for an identified task and Thing. Ambiguous requests require a follow-up. Scheduling is left to the user, with no invented date. At most one Event or Issue creation per message, with completed writes reused on retry.

parameters.description: Suggested maintenance Event requested by the user for a Thing already read.

thingId.description: UUID of the previously read Thing for which the user requested this task.

title.description: Short action title describing the user-requested maintenance or servicing task (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

description.description: Task details and relevant instructions supported by the conversation and retrieved evidence; empty text when no further details are supported. The owner schedules the suggested Event (max 4000 chars).

chatTools.name: create_issue
chatTools.description: Creation of an open Issue requested by the user in the conversation for an identified problem and Thing. A troubleshooting question alone does not request an Issue. Ambiguous requests require a follow-up. At most one Event or Issue creation per message, with completed writes reused on retry.

parameters.description: Open Issue requested by the user for a Thing already read.

thingId.description: UUID of the previously read Thing for which the user requested this Issue.

title.description: Short title describing the user-reported problem to track (min 1 char, max 200 chars).

description.description: Problem details supported by the conversation, such as symptoms, context and troubleshooting already tried, excluding unverified diagnoses; empty text when no further details are supported (max 4000 chars).

chatTools.name: show_cards
chatTools.description: Optional supporting cards for retrieved records. FIELD uses the containing Thing ID and either a registry field address or customFieldId. Repeated entities appear once with all cited pages. Answer text supplies the response to the user.

parameters.description: Previously retrieved resources to cite in the assistant response.

items.description: One interactive citation to a retrieved record, field or attachment.

type.description: Resource kind corresponding to the retrieved resource being cited: THING, FIELD, ATTACHMENT, ISSUE, EVENT or PURCHASABLE.

id.description: UUID copied from tool results: the containing Thing's UUID for FIELD, or the cited resource's UUID for every other type.

fieldSetId.description: Field's set ID copied from the read Thing for FIELD; null for a standalone field or any other card type.

fieldId.description: Registry field ID from the read Thing at the fieldSetId address for FIELD; null for a custom field or another card type.

page.description: One-based page supporting the answer for ATTACHMENT when known; null when the page is unknown or for another card type.

customFieldId.description: Custom field UUID from the read Thing for a FIELD card; fieldId and fieldSetId are null for this address. Null for registry fields and other card types.

cards.description: Up to 12 cards citing resources retrieved in this conversation or returned by a completed write, with resource IDs copied from tool results and only properties relevant to each card type populated.
